title: BitLendingClub launches its Bitcoin lending marketplace
description: BitLendingClub began operating a centrally administered peer-to-peer marketplace matching Bitcoin lenders and borrowers in May 2014.
notes: The reviewed reporting identifies May 2014 but not an exact launch day; 1 May is a sortable approximate date.

title: BitLendingClub adopts the Loanbase name
description: The marketplace changed its public name from BitLendingClub to Loanbase before later returning to the BitLendingClub brand.
notes: September 2015 is supported by contemporaneous retrospective coverage; the exact day and later return date were not established.

title: Attackers compromise BitLendingClub customer accounts
description: Attackers exploited the platform's web stack and gained access to customer accounts, causing confirmed Bitcoin losses among users without two-factor authentication.
notes: Reported loss estimates varied. The incident is not treated as the direct cause of the later regulatory shutdown.

title: BitLendingClub stops new activity and begins shutdown
description: The operator stopped new registrations, loans, and investments and announced a staged closure while existing borrowers continued repayment and customers retained withdrawal access.
notes: The operator expected the wind-down to continue into 2017, but the exact final shutdown and dissolution dates were not verified.

title: Bitbond begins operating a blockchain lending marketplace
description: Bitbond was founded in Berlin in 2013 and began operating a regulated blockchain-based marketplace for small-business loans and global investors.
notes: The first-party company history provides the year but not the exact launch day; 1 January is a sortable approximate date.

title: Bitbond Finance launches the BB1 security-token offering
description: Bitbond Finance introduced the BB1 token, with a stated plan to use a substantial portion of proceeds to finance SME loans originated through Bitbond's global lending platform.
notes: BB1 token rights, issuer obligations, and marketplace lender or borrower claims are separate and are not treated as interchangeable.

title: Bitbond stops new loan origination and pivots to tokenization
description: Bitbond said it had shifted its focus to tokenized securities, returned its asset-broker licence, stopped originating new loans, and would continue administering the existing SME loan portfolio.
notes: The operating company continued as a tokenization provider; this event ends only the product-scoped historical lending-marketplace record.
